critique.pillar: cohort-validity — LLM-circularity of the ground truth
critique.strongest_attack: Every separability/recall/AUC number (AUC 0.55 shared-features, 0.81 concreteness, 2-13% embedding recall, the anti-correlation) is measured against the metaphor_spike apt/inapt cohort, which is 100% Sonnet/Haiku-GENERATED — never human-graded. The whole investigation may be measuring "does context-free data match a Sonnet generator's notion of aptness", not "human aptness". I tested this directly. (1) CIRCULARITY IS REAL AND MATERIAL: on the 4 pairs where Julian's human verdicts overlap the spike labels (topics anchor/ambush), the spike "apt" label and Julian's "live" label AGREE ON ONLY 1 OF 4. Spike calls anchor→stone, ambush→avalanche, ambush→spring "apt"; Julian grades all three DEAD. The spike axis is demonstrably NOT the human live/dead axis. (2) THE HEADLINE "ONE USABLE SIGNAL" INVERTS ON HUMANS: vehicle-concreteness, the investigation's one surviving context-free signal (spike AUC 0.81, which I reproduced at 0.809), scores AUC 0.375 against Julian's actual live/dead labels — it points the WRONG WAY (mean live veh-conc 4.17 < mean dead 4.54). This is exactly the Lakoff cohort-inversion G8 warned about, now confirmed on real human labels. The "concreteness filters candidates" recommendation is built on a spike artifact that does not generalise to the product's own grader. (3) THE GROUND-TRUTH IS THINNER AND MORE DEGENERATE THAN STATED: G4/C4 claim "n=11, 8 live/1 dead/2 null". The actual live grading worktree (.worktrees/next, today's data, which the investigation did NOT read — it read a stale Jun-1 copy) holds 12 distinct graded chains spanning only TWO topics (anchor, ambush), 7 live/5 dead. There is ZERO human signal on the abstract emotion topics (anger, time, hope, grief) that are the Forge's core product and on which all the AUC numbers lean hardest.
critique.evidence: Ran four API-free harnesses (cwd /home/agent/projects/metaforge). (a) inapt_reason_type distribution: single_dimension 53.3% (320), same_domain 27.8% (167), dead_metaphor 11.3% (68), synonym_or_hypernym 4.0%, wrong_concreteness 3.5% [/tmp/cohort_attack.py over metaphor_spike_inapt_phase2_20260525T004154.jsonl]. (b) WITHIN-CLASS vehicle-concreteness AUC (apt vs inapt-of-this-type-only): single_dimension 0.788, same_domain 0.872, dead_metaphor 0.750, synonym_or_hypernym 0.748, wrong_concreteness 0.861 — signal holds in EVERY class, so the 0.81 is NOT an artifact of the inapt generator picking abstract vehicles for one category; rebuts attack (b). Overall reproduced AUC 0.809 (matches reported 0.81). (c) Human cross-validation [/tmp/human_attack.py, /tmp/human_band.py, /tmp/circularity.py over .worktrees/next/.../judgements_provisional.jsonl, latest-wins, 12 chains 7 live/5 dead, topics anchor+ambush]: vehicle-concreteness AUC live-vs-dead = 0.375 (INVERTED); spike-apt vs human-live agree 1/4 on overlapping pairs; human-live pairs share curated features no better than human-dead (live zero-share 1/7, dead 1/5); human-live median embedding rank 390 (recall@200 1/6) vs human-dead median 320 (recall@200 2/4) — dead is CLOSER, so embeddings still fail under human labels. Stale-data check: main checkout judgements file (5576 bytes, Jun 1) has only 3 verdict-bearing records all on topic 'anchor'; live worktree file (11384 bytes, Jun 3) has the 12 cited. synset_concreteness covers 73,927/107,519 synsets.
critique.what_survives: The CORE REFUTATION survives, and is in fact strengthened by the human labels: context-free derivation from the substrate (shared features AND embeddings) cannot separate live from dead metaphor. Under Julian's actual verdicts, shared curated-feature counts do not distinguish live (zero-share 1/7) from dead (1/5), and embedding rank does not either (dead pairs sit closer: median 320 vs live 390). So the conclusion "edges must be LLM-GENERATED, not derived/retrieved" does NOT depend on the spike cohort — it holds on the only human ground truth that exists. The cost conclusion (generation is low-thousands $, ≤4x not binding) is independent of cohort validity entirely (it is direct cost measurement). The reframe that the real bottleneck is QUALITY ADMISSION + thin ground truth is, if anything, vindicated: the human data is so thin (2 topics) and so divergent from the spike (1/4 agreement) that no quantitative quality claim can yet be trusted.
critique.required_fix_or_caveat: The report MUST carry this caveat verbatim-in-spirit: "Every AUC/recall/separability number in this investigation is measured against the Sonnet/Haiku-generated metaphor_spike apt/inapt cohort, NOT human-graded data. On the only overlap with Julian's verdicts (2 topics, 4 pairs), the spike 'apt' label agrees with human 'live' just 1/4 — the spike axis is measurably not the human live/dead axis. Consequence (a): the refutation of DERIVATION is robust — it survives on human labels (features and embeddings fail to separate live from dead under Julian's verdicts too) — so 'edges must be generated, not derived' stands. Consequence (b): the one POSITIVE claim, concreteness as a usable filter (AUC 0.81), is FALSIFIED on human labels (AUC 0.375, inverted) — it is a spike artifact reflecting the abstract-emotion topic mix, and inverts on concrete predatory-action topics exactly as Karpathy Loop-1/G8 predicted. Do NOT ship concreteness as a candidate filter without re-validating on a human-graded cohort that spans the product's topic range. (c) The human ground truth is n=12 over only 2 topics — there is no human signal on abstract emotion topics, which are the Forge's core and where the spike AUCs lean hardest." Also fix the stale-data error: G4/status read the Jun-1 main-checkout judgements (3 records, 1 topic); the live data is in .worktrees/next (12 records, 2 topics) per the deploy-topology note in CLAUDE.md.
critique.could_council_land_this: A SOTA council WOULD land this — it is the most obvious attack on the whole document ("your ground truth is the model grading itself"). Pre-empt it by stating up front, not in a footnote, that (1) the derivation refutation is independently confirmed on human labels (cite the feature/embedding live-vs-dead non-separation: 1/7 vs 1/5 zero-share, median rank 320-dead vs 390-live), so the headline conclusion is NOT circular; and (2) explicitly RETRACT or heavily qualify the concreteness-0.81 finding, conceding it inverts (AUC 0.375) on human labels and is therefore demoted from "the one usable signal" to "a spike-cohort artifact pending human re-validation". The council will also catch the stale-judgements read (investigation cites n=11/8-live on a file that actually has 3 records on 1 topic, while the live n=12/2-topic data sits in .worktrees/next) — fix that proactively. If both are conceded openly, the surviving claim (generate-not-derive, cost-not-binding, quality-admission-is-the-bottleneck) is defensible because it does not rest on the impugned cohort.

critique.pillar: cost-and-judging — cost/feasibility + the hidden judging cost
critique.strongest_attack: The "generation is cheap, ≤4x not binding" headline (status.md, C23, FINDINGS) is built on cost numbers that the investigation's OWN direct measurements falsify by 12-23x, and the synthesis never propagated the correction. (a) Haiku: H-D's $0.005/call is a stale "$2/400-calls" recollection; the orchestrator's own direct probe is $0.062±0.017/call (12.4x higher) — the run log (RL-12) admits this, but status.md C23 still says "low-thousands of $". (b) WORSE and unacknowledged: the cost log now contains a warm Sonnet call at $0.229/call vs H-D's assumed $0.0147 — a 15.6x error — because H-D assumed 790 output tokens when Sonnet actually emits 12,811-14,433 (it writes 10 full chains), a 17x output under-estimate where output is 56-95% of the bill. Corrected 100k 2-call generation = ~$29k, not $1,970 (15x the headline); cold-risk ~$41k. (c) The recommendation admits edges by JUDGING them 'live' over ~600k candidates, a cost the synthesis silently omits. (d) The "≤4x not binding" verdict has NO measured absolute baseline — '1x' is itself computed from the discredited $0.005 rate; re-anchored at direct rates the historical 80k enrichment was ~$5k, so 4x≈$20k, which the $29k 2-call generation alone breaches. So both "cheap" and "≤4x not binding" are unsupported under the project's own direct measurements.
critique.evidence: Read all 6 mandated files + every cost artifact. Direct cost log (artifacts/generation_cost_log.jsonl, 7 rows): Haiku n=5 mean $0.0620±0.0171 (warm 4/5), out_tok mean 5762; Sonnet n=2 = $0.3446 (cold, 12811 out) and $0.2287 (warm, 14433 out). Recomputed: 100k Haiku-only=$6,200; 2-call warm (Haiku+Sonnet-warm)=$29,070; cold=$40,662 — vs H-D/C23 claim $1,970 (15x). Discrepancy factors: Haiku direct/claimed=12.4x; Sonnet-warm direct/claimed=15.6x; root cause = Sonnet output 12811-14433 tok vs H-D-assumed 790 (17.2x), output is 56-95% of Sonnet cost (verified per-row at $15/MTok). JUDGING: 100k x 6 candidates = 600k; warm system-prefix cache_read floor = 36603 tok @ $0.10/MTok = $0.00366/call, so batched-25 judge ≈ $243-404, 1-call-each ≈ $2.5-4.1k, full-Haiku-rate ≈ $37k — judging is real but generation-dominated (verified in Bash). WALL CLOCK: Haiku 53.1s + Sonnet 206.2s/call ⇒ 100k x 2 = 300 days serial; need ~21 concurrent workers for 2wk, 43 for 1wk (computed). 4x anchor: G7 says ≤4x of total project spend; H-D's '1x≈few hundred $' reuses the dead $0.005 rate; re-anchored 80k x $0.062 ≈ $4,960 ⇒ 4x≈$20k < $29k 2-call generation. NOTE: spike apt JSONL has exactly 1 vehicle/topic (it is the deduped apt set), so '~6 vehicles' is the brief's candidate-fan-out figure, not re-derivable from that file — flagged as an assumption, tested at 6/10/40.
critique.what_survives: The DIRECTIONAL conclusion survives: even fully corrected, generation+judging at 100k is ~$6.6k (Haiku-only + batched judge) to ~$29-45k (2-call + judge), i.e. tens-of-thousands of dollars, not the hundreds-of-thousands-to-millions that killed H-B (embedding-band verify at $86k-878k for 50% recall). So generation is still ORDERS cheaper than the rejected derive/retrieve alternatives, and cost is still not the PRIMARY blocker (quality admission + n=11 ground truth is). The judging-cost attack does NOT overturn the recommendation — batched judging (~$250-400) is genuinely cheap because the 57k system-prefix cache_read floor amortises; the cost does move to judging but judging is not where the money is, generation is. The structural finding (edges must be LLM-generated, not derived) is untouched by any cost number.
critique.required_fix_or_caveat: The final report MUST: (1) Replace every instance of "~$2k / low-thousands / $0.005 / $0.0147" with the DIRECT-MEASURED rates: Haiku $0.062/call, Sonnet $0.229/call warm (cold $0.345), driven by ~5.7k/~13k output tokens. State the corrected 100k generation cost as ~$6.2k (Haiku-only) to ~$29k (2-call warm), ~$41k (cold-risk) — NOT $2k. (2) Stop saying "≤4x is not binding" without an absolute baseline; instead state: under direct rates the FULL 2-call pipeline (~$29k) may breach a 4x envelope if the project's true 1x is ~$5-7k, whereas Haiku-only + batched judge (~$6.6k) stays under — so the budget verdict is route-dependent, and the cheap route trades away the Sonnet calibration that uniquely catches dead metaphors (H-D's own quality risk). (3) Add the judging line item explicitly: ~600k candidate edges, batched LLM-judge ~$250-400 (warm, amortised) optimistic / ~$2.5-4k if judged individually — the cost DOES move to judging but is generation-dominated. (4) Add wall-clock/concurrency: ~21-43 concurrent CLI workers needed for a 1-2 week finish; flag this as UNTESTED against CLI rate limits and the assumption that warm cache holds at that concurrency (the warm rate is n=4 Haiku / n=1 Sonnet — thin). (5) Carry the n: Sonnet warm rate is n=1; treat $0.229 as a point estimate needing replication before any budget commitment.
critique.could_council_land_this: YES — a SOTA council would land this hard and fast: the contradiction is sitting in the investigation's own committed artifact (RL-12 logs the 12x Haiku discrepancy AND a warm-Sonnet $0.229 row exists in the cost log) while status.md C23 still prints "low-thousands of $". A reviewer opening generation_cost_log.jsonl recomputes ~$29k in one line and asks why the synthesis says $2k. The 17x Sonnet-output assumption error in hd_routing_cost_harness.py (CONTENT['sonnet']['out']=790 vs measured ~13000) is a single grep. Pre-empt by: (a) regenerating all cost figures FROM generation_cost_log.jsonl, not from H-D's stale anchors, and deleting the $0.005/$0.0147 numbers from the synthesis; (b) stating the honest range $6.6k-$45k with the n=1 Sonnet-warm caveat; (c) reframing the headline from "cheap / ≤4x not binding" to "tens-of-thousands, orders cheaper than derive/retrieve, route- and concurrency-dependent — and STILL not the primary blocker (quality admission + n=11 is)" — which is both defensible and preserves the actual decision-relevant conclusion.

critique.pillar: recommendation-responsiveness — does the recommendation actually deliver HIGH-QUALITY edges at 100k
critique.strongest_attack:
The recommendation does not answer the mission — it RENAMES the mission and punts it. The mission demands HIGH-QUALITY context-free edges (graded `live`, linkage-good, context-free) at 100k. The recommendation ("generate cheaply with Haiku/Sonnet + concreteness pre-filter + a live/dead judge calibrated to Julian's grading") delivers only CANDIDATES. Every quality property in the bar is met exclusively AFTER the judge runs — and the judge is the one component that (a) does not exist, (b) has never been validated, and (c) is the actual hard problem. Concretely:

1. NO JUDGE EXISTS. There is no `build_judge_prompt` anywhere in the codebase (grep returns zero definitions). The only committed "quality at scale" instrument, `grading_diagnostics.py`, tracks a `bad_path` rate that is not even in the current verdict model — run against the real human data it CRASHES (`KeyError: 'label'`) because the labels are `live/dead/null`. So the load-bearing component of the recommendation is unbuilt, and the closest existing artifact is wired to the wrong schema.

2. THE QUALITY EVIDENCE IS 2 TOPICS, NOT 11 CHAINS. The headline "8/11 live" implies Sonnet generation clears Julian's bar. But the 11 human-graded chains cover exactly TWO distinct topics: anxiety (5) and anchor (6). The other 18 of 20 generated topics (anger, time, grief, hope, courage, recursion, gridlock...) have ZERO human verdicts. 5.5% of generated chains are judged, over 10% of topics. There is NO evidence Sonnet meets the live bar at acceptable rate across the topic space — the recommendation rests on n=2-topics generalised to 100k.

3. THE PRE-FILTER IS BLIND TO THE #1 FAILURE MODE. The concreteness gradient (the only surviving context-free signal, AUC 0.81) has dead-metaphor sub-AUC 0.608, and at 70% apt recall it KEEPS 54% of dead metaphors (measured: dead_kept_frac 0.541). Dead/conventional metaphor is the product's primary exclusion target. The pipeline therefore has NO context-free defence against dead metaphors — the entire dead/live decision is offloaded to the nonexistent judge. The pre-filter screens structural junk (synonyms, same-domain: AUC 0.84-0.88) but waves through exactly what the product must reject.

4. THE FRAMING IS WRONG. The investigation correctly DIAGNOSES that the bottleneck is QUALITY ADMISSION + thin ground truth (n=11), then issues a recommendation headlined "Do not derive — GENERATE." That is answering a question (is generation cheap? yes) that the same report proves is NOT binding. The honest recommendation, given its own evidence, is: "the deliverable is blocked on the JUDGE/eval loop; invest in scaling the grading tool (more human labels across all topics + an LLM-judge validated against them) BEFORE committing to a 100k generation pass." Generation is the cheap, solved part; the report leads with it anyway.
critique.evidence:
All checks reproducible on the committed data:

- HUMAN GROUND TRUTH (data-pipeline/grading/judgements_provisional.jsonl, latest-wins by chain_signature): 11 distinct chains, labels {live:8, dead:1, null:2}, confidence {high:10, med:1}, ALL judged_by=julian, ALL round=1. Distinct TOPICS = 2 (anxiety:5, anchor:6). Generated population (sonnet_chains_provisional_r1.jsonl) = 200 chains over 20 topics → judged fraction 11/200 = 5.5%, topic coverage 2/20.

- NO JUDGE: `grep -rn build_judge_prompt data-pipeline/` returns nothing. `metaphor_graph.py` only has a `record_judgment` DB-insert (label CHECK in {live,dead_synonym,dead_lakoff,irrelevant,edge_case}) — no LLM judge, no agreement metric (no cohen/kappa/confusion anywhere in scripts/ except unrelated). grading_diagnostics.py `convergence_verdict` tracks `bad_path` only; run on real data → `KeyError: 'label'` (the 2 null records) and would in any case find 0 bad_path → INSUFFICIENT.

- DEAD-METAPHOR BLINDNESS (artifacts/hc_multivariate_result.json): per_inapt_class_auc.dead_metaphor = 0.608; dead_leakage_vs_apt_recall at target_apt_recall 0.5/0.7/0.9 → dead_kept_frac 0.377/0.541/0.721. Concreteness-only AUC 0.812 (separability_result.txt) confirms the pre-filter ≈ one feature.

- COST GROUNDING SOFTER THAN HEADLINED: the investigation's OWN measured Sonnet cost (artifacts/sonnet_cost_result.txt) = $0.143–$0.229/call warm (mean $0.186), which is 12.7× the $0.0147/call H-D used to claim "~$2k baseline." Recomputing with measured warm rates: Haiku $0.054 + Sonnet $0.186 = $0.24/topic → 100k 2-call baseline ≈ $24k (not ~$2k). Adding the judging the recommendation requires (~10 candidate edges/topic): batched-optimistic +$2k, per-edge-haiku-warm +$54k → total envelope ~$26k–$78k. Still plausibly inside ≤4× of historical enrichment spend, but an order of magnitude above the "$2k, spend is not the constraint" headline.
critique.what_survives:
The core NEGATIVE results survive intact and are not what I am attacking: context-free DERIVATION/RETRIEVAL of edges from the substrate is genuinely dead (shared-features ~chance, embeddings anti-correlated, recall ~2%, symmetry/transitivity invalid — all independently replicated). The conclusion "you cannot avoid per-topic LLM generation" holds. The diagnosis that the binding constraint is QUALITY ADMISSION + thin ground truth (n=11) is CORRECT and is the report's most valuable finding.

What survives of the recommendation: generation is the right MECHANISM (nothing cheaper works), and the concreteness gradient is a legitimate FREE verification-volume pre-filter for structural junk. So "generate, don't derive" is correct as far as it goes. It just is not a delivery plan for HIGH-QUALITY edges — it is a plan to produce candidates plus a promissory note for the judge that does the actual quality work.
critique.required_fix_or_caveat:
The final report MUST reframe and carry these caveats explicitly:

1. RECOMMENDATION RESTATED: the deliverable is NOT "generate" — generation is the cheap/solved part. The recommendation must be "the path to 100k high-quality edges is GATED ON BUILDING AND VALIDATING THE JUDGE; invest in the human+LLM grading loop FIRST." Generation is necessary but not sufficient; it produces candidates, and quality is conferred only by an admission judge that does not yet exist.

2. EXPLICIT NON-CLAIM: state that the pipeline currently has ZERO context-free defence against dead/conventional metaphors (concreteness keeps 54% of dead at 70% recall), so dead-metaphor rejection is 100% dependent on the unbuilt judge. Do not let the concreteness pre-filter be read as a quality gate — it is a volume gate for structural junk only.

3. GROUND-TRUTH HONESTY: the only quality evidence (8/11 live) covers 2 of 20 topics. The report must NOT imply Sonnet generation meets Julian's bar at scale. The immediate next action is to grade across all 20 topics (and ideally a fresh cohort), not to launch a 100k pass.

4. JUDGE-FIRST GATE: name a hard prerequisite — an LLM-judge validated to acceptable agreement against an EXPANDED human set (n≫11, spanning topics) — before any 100k commitment. Quantify the judge's own cost as part of the recommendation (it is ~$2k–$54k depending on batching, not free), and fix the cost headline using the MEASURED Sonnet rate ($0.186/call → ~$24k generation alone), retiring the stale ~$2k figure.

5. The judging cost "just relocates the bottleneck" risk flagged in status.md is REAL and must be resolved in the report, not left open: judging ~1M candidate edges with a judge whose precision is unknown (n=11) is the actual mission risk.
critique.could_council_land_this: YES — a SOTA council would land all four sub-attacks easily because the evidence is in the committed data and the recommendation's own headline contradicts its own diagnosis. The single most quotable kill-shot: "the report concludes the bottleneck is QUALITY ADMISSION via a judge, then recommends GENERATE — and the judge it depends on does not exist (no build_judge_prompt), has never been validated, and the only quality evidence is 8/11 chains spanning 2 topics." Pre-empt by: (a) re-titling the recommendation around the judge/grading-loop investment, not generation; (b) adding an explicit "what is NOT yet validated" section listing the absent judge, the 2-topic ground truth, and the dead-metaphor blind spot; (c) replacing the ~$2k cost headline with the measured ~$24k generation + judging envelope and stating ≤4× is non-binding only IF historical spend baseline is correctly stated; (d) stating a concrete judge-first gate with a falsifiable agreement threshold against an expanded human set. If the report instead leads with "generation is cheap, ship it," the council will correctly call it a recommendation that punts the hard problem and dresses up a candidate-generator as an edge-delivery plan.

critique.pillar: completeness-and-missed — what plausible in-constraint approach the investigation never explored
critique.strongest_attack: "You concluded edges can't be DERIVED from the substrate after testing only feature-overlap and FastText embeddings — but the database ships a `relations` table with 234,810 WordNet structural rows (hypernym/hyponym arms rt=1/2 at 88,075 each, meronym/holonym rt=11/12, similar/domain arms) that you NEVER QUERIED. G1 names only the metonym_of/antonym_of arms; H-F tested symmetry/transitivity of GENERATED edges, not WordNet relation traversal. The taxonomic backbone is exactly the structured substrate a 'context-free edge' should exploit, and you dismissed it by silence. Separately, you fixed the target at '100k topics' and built every cost/coverage number on it without ever checking how many synsets users can actually query: only ~13,800 lemmas are mid-frequency (zipf>=3 -> 35,832 synsets; zipf>=4 -> 18,873). The frequencies table was in the DB the whole time. If the real target is the frequency-weighted top ~15-35k, your cost math is 3-7x too high and your already-generated 200-topic seed covers ~1.5% of the real target, not the 0.2% implied by 100k — which reframes the whole conclusion from 'must generate 100k' to 'keep generating against a much smaller, query-weighted frontier you're already 1.5% into.'"
critique.evidence: Ran SQL/python on data-pipeline/output/lexicon_v2.db (2026-05-26). (a) `relations` table = 234,810 rows; relation_type codes decoded by sampling: rt=1/2 hypernym/hyponym (88,075 each; entity->physical entity), rt=11/12 meronym/holonym (cell->organism), rt=40 similar/derivational (23,176), rt=50 adj-similar, rt=60 derivational (able->ability), rt=91/92 domain. This table is grep-absent from the entire investigation (only `_gloss`, antonym_of, metonym_of appear). I tested 7 canonical live pairs for relation connectivity: time->river, hope->horizon, anger->volcano, idea->light, life->journey, grief->ocean ALL have 0 direct + 0 two-hop relation paths; anger->fire's only link is a verb-sense collision (synset 'make angry' <-> 'call forth emotions'), NOT the combustion noun -> 0/7 genuine recoveries. (b) every synset has non-empty `definition` (107,519/107,519); spike records carry `_gloss` (198/200); gloss used only as generation input (build_apt_prompt(t,gloss)), never as a standalone cheaper proposer. (c) apt cohort = 200 distinct topics, 1112 (topic,vehicle) pairs, 571 distinct vehicles already generated. (e) `frequencies` table = 127,311 rows; zipf>=3 -> 13,800 lemmas / 35,832 synsets; zipf>=4 -> 4,108 lemmas / 18,873 synsets; zipf>=5 -> 5,736 synsets. No file in the investigation mentions frequency/zipf/query-weighting/top-N.
critique.what_survives: The CORE conclusion survives intact and is even strengthened on the derivation axis: I empirically confirmed WordNet relations recover 0/7 live metaphor pairs (the one apparent hit is a sense artifact), for the identical mechanistic reason as feature-overlap and embeddings — relations encode WITHIN-domain taxonomic similarity, and live metaphor is a cross-domain leap. So 'edges cannot be derived/retrieved from the existing substrate' holds across all FOUR substrates now (features, embeddings, relations, glosses-as-static-features). 'Generation is cheap; <=4x not binding' survives (a smaller target only makes it cheaper). 'Quality admission + thin n=11 ground truth is the real bottleneck' survives and is the right headline. The gloss and seed-reuse points are consistent with the existing 'generate, don't derive' recommendation, not counter to it.
critique.required_fix_or_caveat: The final report MUST add two caveats. (1) RELATIONS: explicitly state the WordNet `relations` table (234,810 rows; hypernym/meronym/similar arms) was tested as a context-free edge substrate and recovers 0/7 canonical live pairs (only sense-collision noise), failing on the same within-domain-similarity mechanism as features/embeddings — do NOT leave it as silent dismissal, or the council lands 'you ignored the structural graph you already have.' (2) TARGET SIZING: stop asserting '100k' as the requirement. State that the frequency-weighted queryable frontier is ~15-35k synsets (zipf>=3->35.8k, zipf>=4->18.9k via the `frequencies` table), which (a) cuts all generation cost 3-7x and (b) makes the existing 200-topic / 1112-pair seed ~1.5% of a realistic target — reframing the path as 'keep the bootstrap loop running against a query-weighted frontier' rather than 'generate 100k.' Optionally note gloss-only Haiku as an untested cheaper-generation variant (does not change the conclusion). None of this overturns the headline; it hardens it.
critique.could_council_land_this: YES on the unqualified version — a SOTA council reading G1 ('three of four arms derived combinatorially') plus a schema dump showing a 234,810-row `relations` table and a 127,311-row `frequencies` table the investigation never queried would land 'you declared derivation impossible without testing the WordNet structural arms or checking whether 100k is even the right N.' Pre-empt by landing the 0/7-relations measurement and the zipf target-sizing numbers IN the report (both reproducible in <2 min of SQL, both done above), converting two silent omissions into two explicit, evidenced negative results. The relations check in particular flips a potential 'sloppy completeness' strike into a fifth corroborating data point for the central thesis.
